lines.text: Clara has come to live in a tall house full of music. Before she may play a single note, the Butler asks her to sit down.

Then he shows her, one thing at a time. Sit on the front half of the stool. Feet flat on the floor. Back tall, shoulders soft. And the stool just high enough that your forearms are level with the keys, like a table top.
Now, at the piano. Sit at the piano and check the four things, one by one: front half, feet flat, back tall, arms level with the keys.
And here is how it ended.
Nearly two hundred years ago another girl called Clara, Clara Wieck, played in public for the first time, at the Gewandhaus concert hall in Leipzig. She was nine years old.
She grew up to be one of the great pianists of her time, Clara Schumann. She, too, had to start at the beginning.
One more thing to try. Sit at the piano and check three things before you play: feet flat, back tall, arms level with the keys.
That night, from the empty music room, Clara heard a single note. When she looked, all eighty-eight keys lay perfectly still. Which one had it been?
